problem_trigger: The P05 assignment released by PR #131 was later diagnosed as aged_no_candidate/did_not_materialize from PR visibility even though Operator A had already produced a retrievable producer-ready branch and commit 622456e9ee35613b2a31c0efcfb90725dc1570d8. This caused a false producer-nonperformance diagnosis and risked duplicate research.
prior_design: Controller reconciliation relied too heavily on visible PR state to infer whether assigned producer work existed. Producer branch/SHA handoff status was not durably required in controller state, and C premise checking did not catch the incorrect non-materialization premise before later recovery.
hypothesis_rationale: Requiring producer-visibility reconciliation across recent producer outputs, branches, commits/SHAs, PRs, and task references before declaring no_candidate or allocating replacement work should distinguish handoff/observability failure from producer non-performance and prevent unnecessary research redo.
exact_change: Within existing ordinary-management authority, the human-approved producer-visibility/recovery gate now requires D to inspect live producer evidence before no_candidate/abandonment/replacement decisions; producer-ready work without a PR is classified HANDOFF_BLOCKED and preserved/recovered by exact branch/SHA. Controller state must retain branch/SHA/PR handoff status for active Tier-2 work. For P05 specifically, D recovered commit 622456e9ee35613b2a31c0efcfb90725dc1570d8 rather than redoing research, restored it through PR #137, routed the refreshed exact candidate through CI and independent C review, and integrated it as canonical main 7e73a5458c35022bbfff2ecf78325385cf071227 after C PASS.
expected_benefit: Prevent false producer-nonperformance diagnoses caused by missing PR handoff.
Recover producer-ready work instead of duplicating research.
Make assignment-to-producer-ready-to-PR-to-C-to-D flow observable by exact branch/SHA/PR.
Improve premise checking before controller replacement decisions.
risks: Branch/SHA reconciliation can add controller toil if performed mechanically rather than when assignment status is ambiguous.
Old branches can be mistaken for current candidates without task/portfolio and commit-context checks.
Durable handoff metadata can become stale unless post-integration coherence removes completed work.
evaluation_window: Next 6-12 healthy controller cycles and any future assignment with missing or delayed PR handoff.
evaluation_criteria: No producer assignment is classified no_candidate/did_not_materialize solely from absent PR state.
Producer-ready orphan branches are recovered without research redo when not superseded on evidence.
Active Tier-2 controller records contain exact producer branch/SHA/PR handoff status.
Replacement allocations occur only after producer-visibility reconciliation or explicit evidence-based supersession.
Recovery/observability toil does not dominate roughly half of controller capacity across three windows.

observed_outcomes.observation: Operator A producer work existed at branch operator-a/p05-parent-messaging-exposure-test-20260911 and commit 622456e9ee35613b2a31c0efcfb90725dc1570d8 despite the prior no-candidate diagnosis.
The missing producer-to-PR/controller handoff was recovered without redoing P05 research; refreshed PR #137 received exact-head CI and independent C PASS and was integrated.
PR-only reconciliation had misdiagnosed the event, and prior C premise checking did not identify that producer-ready work already existed.

The failure was primarily handoff/observability and premise-checking failure, not producer non-performance. Branch/SHA visibility is therefore a higher-value control than adding more producer research or more scheduler activity.

failures_side_effects: Several controller windows were spent holding, diagnosing, and recovering work that had already been produced.
The false no-candidate lesson persisted in controller reasoning until explicit producer-visibility reconciliation corrected it.
The mandatory causal checkpoint itself became overdue and held new Tier-2 production after P05 integration.
lessons: PR absence is not evidence of producer non-performance.
Before replacement allocation, reconcile producer outputs, branches, exact SHAs, PRs, and task references.
Preserve orphaned producer-ready work and recover the handoff; do not delete/reset or redo it merely because a PR is missing.
C verification should challenge controller premises about candidate provenance/status as well as substantive claims when those premises affect whether work is reviewed.
Keep handoff visibility minimal and durable; do not solve observability failures by expanding scheduler authority or adding coordination layers.
